ForeSpark realizes WCS with (i) a context-aware pre-draft estimator that predicts acceptance for every candidate length from the target model's context features, (ii) a lightweight joint draft-verify scheduler that selects both lengths through a global sort, and (iii) a post-draft budget distribution that spends verification on the most promising tokens. Implemented on vLLM, ForeSpark improves throughput by up to 1.77x over the state-of-the-art DSpark and by 2.49x over autoregressive decoding at a matched per-request generation rate, without changing the output distribution. It also tolerates higher load, sustaining up to 1.51x the request rate of DSpark under latency service level objectives (SLOs).

papers.title: Regularity Estimates for a Nonhomogeneous Free Boundary Interface Problem
papers.abstract: In this work, we establish regularity properties for minimizers of a novel nonhomogeneous interface problem with a free boundary, formulated in Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. The nonlinear terms fulfill Lieberman-type structural assumptions with subcritical growth. The principal difficulties stem from the nonhomogeneous framework and the lack of suitable representation formulas. Our findings extend recent contributions in the field and provide new insights even in the particular case of the Laplacian. Keywords: Free Boundary Problems; Orlicz-Spaces; Nonhomogeneous Operator; Transmission Problem; Regularity.

papers.title: Giant Graviton Correlators: From Non-maximal to Dual, Bootstrap and Hidden Symmetry
papers.abstract: We compute four-point functions of two light $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS operators and two heavy giant graviton operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills theory at large $N$ and infinite 't Hooft coupling. Using bootstrap techniques, we determine the correlators for arbitrary light-operator dimensions and arbitrary allowed sizes of non-maximal sphere and dual giant gravitons. We show that these correlators exhibit a hidden ten-dimensional conformal symmetry, allowing them to be organized into compact generating functions. Remarkably, the generating functions for both types of giant gravitons can be obtained from the maximal giant case through $SO(2,10)$ rotations in the embedding space.

papers.title: G-radical-square-zero algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first provide necessary and sufficient conditions for a Krull-Schmidt triangulated category with Auslander-Reiten triangles to have square-zero radical. One of these conditions is that the middle term of every Auslander-Reiten triangle is either zero or indecomposable. We then call an artin algebra {\it G-radical-square-zero} if the stable category of Gorenstein-projective modules has square-zero radical. We characterize when a G-radical-square-zero algebra is CM-finite and, in this case, give an additive generator of the stable category. For certain Iwanaga-Gorenstein G-radical-square-zero algebras, we further show that the stable category admits an additive generator consisting of higher syzygies of simple modules.

papers.title: Differential Monodromy, $q$-Opers, and Universal $(G,q)$-Wronskians
papers.abstract: We give a geometric formulation of the $q$DE/ODE/IM correspondence for families of differential operators associated with simple Lie algebras of ADE type. Under analytic hypotheses, the $q$-connection associated with shifted monodromy defines a twisted $(G,q)$-oper and has Steinberg form in the frame of solutions normalized by prescribed asymptotics in a sector at infinity. We identify the central connection between the normalized solution frames at zero and infinity with a universal meromorphic $(G,q)$-Wronskian. Its generalized minors give $Q$-functions satisfying the ADE $QQ$-relations. When $q$ is not a root of unity, we parametrize shifted monodromy by quantum-affine $q$-characters evaluated on shifted $Q$-ratios, using the same character formulas that describe normalized transfer-matrix eigenvalues. We verify the analytic hypotheses for generic untwisted Feigin--Frenkel--Hernandez affine opers, thereby relating these affine opers to twisted $(G,q)$-opers.

papers.title: Double-quantum enhanced coherent control and magnetic sensing of spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride
papers.abstract: The negatively charged boron vacancy ($V_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is a promising spin defect for quantum sensing in two-dimensional material systems. Previous hBN experiments have mainly exploited the two spin-triplet ground-state single-quantum transitions separately. Here we implement a double-quantum driving scheme based on simultaneous resonant microwave excitation of both ground-state single-quantum transitions, establishing coherent control of the $Δm_s=2$ manifold in a $V_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$ ensemble. We compare the resulting double-quantum response with the corresponding single-quantum protocol under identical experimental conditions. The double-quantum protocol enhances the optical readout contrast and yields a 2.6-fold signal-to-noise improvement in AC magnetometry. We further use the double-quantum relaxation channel as a differential probe of electric-field and strain noise, showing that the present data are compatible with correlated-surface or volume-distributed fluctuations, while short-range uncorrelated surface-noise models are disfavored within the assumptions of our analysis. These results establish double-quantum coherent control and frequency-resolved AC magnetometry in hBN spin ensembles, and identify the sample-dependent measurements needed to determine the microscopic origin of the dominant relaxation channels.

papers.title: Fermat ProbCover: Coverage-Based Active Learning on Fermat Distance Graphs
papers.abstract: Active learning aims to reduce annotation cost by selecting the most informative examples for labeling. In the low-budget regime, where uncertainty-based methods often fail, coverage-based active learning methods such as ProbCover have been shown to be effective. However, these methods typically rely on Euclidean distance, which may not adequately capture the underlying geometry of data. In this article, we propose PC-Fermat, a coverage-based active learning method that replaces Euclidean coverage neighborhoods with neighborhoods defined by a Fermat distance, i.e., a data-adaptive distance that reflects the underlying distribution of the data points. To facilitate computation, we construct a weighted Euclidean neighborhood graph and use a truncated shortest-path algorithm to compute the Fermat coverage graph. We also establish sufficient conditions under which this construction exactly preserves the Fermat coverage computed on the complete graph. Finally, we evaluate PC-Fermat on eight classification datasets across varying labeling budgets, with particular emphasis on the very low-budget regime. Our experimental results demonstrate that PC-Fermat outperforms several existing active learning methods on the majority of the datasets.

papers.title: Complete Decentralization of Wave Equation Control on a Compact Domain
papers.abstract: A feedback control policy is completely decentralized if the actuation signal at each location in space can be computed based only on state information from that location. For systems equipped with large numbers of spatially distributed sensors and actuators, completely decentralized controllers are desirable since they can be implemented in a communication and computation efficient manner, but generally perform worse than centralized counterparts. However, through a case study of Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) design for wave dynamics on a compact spatial domain, we show that careful design of system parameters to satisfy certain conditions causes a decentralized control policy to perform as well as any centralized policy. We then propose a spatially filtered $H_2$ norm to show that satisfying these conditions does not inherently degrade achievable closed-loop system performance, enabling simultaneous realization of both desirable performance and communication/computation efficiency via system-control co-design. Additional robustness analysis characterizes a range of system parameters such that the system interconnected with a decentralized controller maintains stability and near-optimal performance. Although our framework is derived for spatially continuous dynamics, we demonstrate that this theory can be leveraged to derive results for decentralization in finite-dimensional settings through a damped mass-spring example.

papers.title: Feedback Design in the Shadow of Strategic Communication
papers.abstract: We study optimal feedback design when evaluations affect subsequent strategic communication within organizations. A firm designs public feedback about an employee's potential before the employee communicates private information about project-specific circumstances to a manager. While more informative feedback helps the manager make better decisions, it can also intensify preference conflicts and undermine the credibility of subsequent communication. We characterize the optimal feedback policy. First, full disclosure is either optimal for all prior beliefs or strictly suboptimal for all of them. In particular, it is optimal when preference conflicts are sufficiently small or sufficiently large. Second, when full disclosure is suboptimal, no disclosure is optimal for some priors, while partial disclosure is strictly optimal for some priors if and only if the number of messages in equilibrium communication varies with posterior beliefs. Third, optimal partial disclosure can conclusively identify low-potential employees when high potential is rare, but high-potential employees when it is common.

papers.title: Economics of Selection in Ranking & Selection: Neither Fixed-Precision nor Fixed-Budget
papers.abstract: Ranking and selection (R&S) has evolved tremendously over the last several decades, with applications in agriculture, discrete optimization with computer simulation, clinical trial design, and other areas. We challenge a widely accepted classification of R&S procedures into two categories: fixed-precision and fixed-budget. We discuss a third class, economics-of-selection (EoS) procedures, which is conceptually distinct and is found in the extant literature on Bayesian hypothesis testing and simulation optimization. Procedures in this third class seek to optimally balance two quantities: the cost of learning about the performance of each alternative and the quality of the alternative ultimately selected on the basis of that learning. Fixed-precision and fixed-budget procedures tend to optimize one of these quantities while constraining the other. We clarify these differences and show why they matter. We then present new frequentist R&S procedures in this third category, including both two-stage procedures and a sequential heuristic, assuming Gaussian observations with either known or unknown variances. We find that EoS is not a question of Bayesian versus frequentist analysis, asymptotic versus finite-sample analysis, finite-stage versus fully sequential procedures, or comparing one mean with a standard versus comparing multiple alternatives. We identify opportunities for further R&S research.

papers.title: SLIC: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning Small LMs for Multi-Turn Analog Circuit Optimization
papers.abstract: Analog integrated circuit (IC) design is a multi-turn, simulator-grounded engineering task that demands iterative reasoning over coupled performance tradeoffs, yet proprietary process design kits (PDKs) make hosted large language model workflows difficult to deploy in practical design settings. We present SLIC (Small LM Iterating on Circuits), a reinforcement fine-tuning framework that trains a 4B-scale, locally deployable language model for closed-loop analog circuit optimization. SLIC pairs structured circuit representations with discretized relative-update actions, domain- and success-gated multiobjective rewards, and Reward-Guided Rollout Steering (RGRS), which turns per-step simulator feedback into signals for both policy learning and online rollout construction in this sparse, highly constrained domain. We further release an open, goal-conditioned benchmark of 41 amplifier topologies with standardized protocols for in-distribution validation, held-out topology evaluation, and cross-technology-node transfer. Trained solely with open source 65 nm CMOS predictive technology models (PTM), SLIC-Random achieves 87.1% in-distribution four-specification Pass@1 within eight turns, surpassing the 763B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Think by 48.5 percentage points. Beyond the training distribution, SLIC-Softmax reaches 72.6% Pass@1 on held-out topologies, and the trained policies consistently transfer across five unseen technology nodes without additional fine-tuning. This transfer extends to a commercial TSMC 65 nm CMOS PDK, where SLIC-Random achieves 49.9% held-out-topology Pass@1, demonstrating practical deployment through local inference without transmitting proprietary data to external LLM services. Performance further scales with test-time simulator interactions, reaching up to 83.2% held-out-topology Pass@1 at a 32-turn budget.

papers.title: Camera3R: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Heterogeneous Camera Models
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction (3R) from unconstrained multi-view images has recently emerged as a prominent research direction in 3D computer vision. Various foundational reconstruction models have been proposed with different architectures and reconstruction paradigms. Despite being trained on large-scale perspective datasets with substantial computational resources, these models generally struggle to generalize to non-perspective images. This limitation hinders their deployment in applications involving arbitrary, unknown, and potentially heterogeneous camera models. To build on the capabilities of existing reconstruction models with minimal retraining, we propose Camera3R, a low-rank adaptation framework that efficiently extends perspective-pretrained 3R networks to any other camera models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, with only 0.5% additional parameters and less than a day of training, Camera3R adapts a foundational 3D reconstruction model to non-perspective cameras while fully preserving its original performance on perspective inputs. Code is available at https://github.com/android-xr/camera3r.

papers.title: SafeRoute-MAS: Coverage-Aware and Risk-Calibrated Message Routing for Multi-Agent Scientific Reasoning
papers.abstract: We introduce SafeRoute-MAS, a coverage-aware, risk-calibrated procedure that keeps all specialist messages or removes one using only pre-integration information. On a sealed cache of 5,328 committees, its source-compatible operating point gains +1.80 percentage points (95% CI [+1.13, +2.52]) while removing 12.76% of message tokens. We also run 4,580 controlled integrations over a stratified 458-committee sample on a public gpt-oss-120b endpoint. The sample estimate is -0.09 points; design weighting to the original workload gives +0.94 points (95% CI [-1.31, +3.50]) and 18.72% acted-input reduction. A weighted token-matched comparison likewise does not establish a selector advantage (+1.68 points, CI [-1.27, +5.10]). Only 13 of 88 cached non-neutral labels (14.8%) retain direction by repeated-call majority. Expected-corruption UCL is 4.60% after weighting, but only 2 of 11 prespecified marginals pass the support/risk rule. We therefore propose a numerical qualification with Keep-All fallback, applied here retrospectively rather than validated prospectively.

papers.title: Divisibility graphs of semigroups as weighted poset blow-ups
papers.abstract: We develop a structural theory of divisibility graphs of arbitrary semigroups. For a semigroup $S$, let $S/{\mathcal J}$ be the poset of Green's ${\mathcal J}$-classes ordered by inclusion of principal ideals,and equip each $\mathcal {J}$-class $J$ with the weight $|J|$. We prove that the divisibility graph ${\operatorname{Div}}(S)$ is obtained from the comparability directed graph $Comp(S/{\mathcal J})$ by replacing each $\mathcal J$-class with a complete symmetric graph of order $|J|$ and by replacing each directed edge $J_u$ to $J_v$ in $Comp(S/{\mathcal J})$ with all directed edges from every element of $J_u$ to every element of $J_v$. Consequently, ${\operatorname{Div}}(S)$ is determined, up to isomorphism, by the weighted poset $(S/\mathcal {J},\{ J \}_{J\in S/{\mathcal J}})$. This yields structural descriptions of its strongly connected components, maximal unilaterally connected subgraphs. The main contribution is the reduction of divisibility graph problems to weighted quotient-poset problems. As applications, we obtain reconstruction and isomorphism criteria and prove an inheritance theorem for divisibility $D$-saturated subsemigroups.

papers.title: When Reasoning looks like Hidden Understanding: How Chain-of-Thought Fosters Anthropomorphism, Perceptions of Epistemic Superiority, and Cognitive Deference
papers.abstract: As AI-based products permeate society, specifically systems using generative models, a belief system is emerging about what these products are and what they can and cannot do. One common belief concerns the perception of the form of language as evidence of 'understanding' language. As these generative models reproduce linguistic patterns rather than understand meaning, interpreting these patterns as evidence of understanding is a misattribution. This misconception is extended by the notion that generative models can 'explain their reasoning.' Anecdotally, these misconceptions which mistake the form of language for its meaning are driving cognitive deference to AI systems in a way that displaces human agency. Such mistakes involve attributions of cognitive properties to the system, allowing them to be treated like intentional 'minds'. Importantly, perceived epistemic authority and superiority make that 'mind' worth deferring to. Anthropomorphism in tandem with epistemic authority and superiority, we argue, increases the risk that users generalise from narrow task performance to broader competencies, committing the "fallacy of composition". This paper explores misconceptions of Chain of Thought (CoT) reasoning as sufficient transparent 'explanation'. We explore how anthropomorphism acts as a vehicle for cognitive deference of decision-making and perceptions of epistemic superiority in AI systems. Finally, we explore CoT's ramifications using medicine as an example. Taken together, we conclude that explainability operationalised through CoT is highly problematic and undercuts the very ethical principles it is intended to serve. While CoT may be valuable for improving output accuracy and moderation, we suggest that the practice of asking models to provide user facing reasons for their outputs should be actively discouraged, and AI literacy training should explicitly caution against its use.

papers.title: Deep Personalization: Continuous Context Observation for Local Proactive Agents
papers.abstract: As AI agents become increasingly capable, users must still recognize when and how to ask for help, leaving many opportunities for useful support unrealized. Proactive agents hold the promise to close this gap, but effective proactivity requires understanding users' real-time activities and personalizing intervention timing so that assistance is offered when it is likely to be helpful rather than disruptive. We introduce deep personalization, a closed-loop process that connects continuous context observation with continual agent adaptation: an agent observes user activity, selectively retains long-term context, and adapts intervention decisions from implicit feedback. We initiate deep personalization in Coco, a proactive desktop agent, by having a separate Observer Agent that monitors desktop activity, maintains compact long-term user modeling context, and learns when assistance is desirable from implicit signals such as engagement, dismissal, explicit requests, and repeated work patterns. We further develop efficient on-device strategies to enable the Observer Agent to run on local AI compute platforms without streaming raw activity data off-device. For evaluation at scale without collecting sensitive real-user activity, we introduce a data-synthesis pipeline that transforms existing computer-use trajectories into OSWorld-Persona, a benchmark with persona-conditioned intervention labels. On OSWorld-Persona, deep personalization improves macro F1 across three model backbones from 0.12-0.19 under direct prompting to 0.35-0.48 after adaptation, a 2.4-3.0x relative gain. In a week-long user study, we observe that Coco improves its macro-averaged F1 score from 0.199 to 0.515. These results suggest that on-device deep personalization can make proactive agents more timely and increasingly aligned with each user's everyday work.

papers.title: Surface subgroups with prescribed finite quotients
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite quotient of a finite covolume Kleinian group $G$ can be realized by a surface subgroup. More precisely, given an epimorphism from $G$ onto a finite group $F$, there exists a surface subgroup that maps surjectively onto $F$. As a consequence, the union of the surface subgroups is dense in $G$ with respect to the profinite topology. We also apply this result to obtain more examples of atoroidal surface bundles with signature zero in the construction of Kent--Leininger.

papers.title: Bounding the security of the Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash function
papers.abstract: The Bromberg-Shpilrain-Vdovina hash functions are a family of Cayley hash functions indexed by an integer parameter $k\ge 2$. Hashes are matrices in $SL_2(p)$ where $p$ is a large prime. We present an attack which finds collisions of length $O(\log p)$ whose average-case time complexity is $O(p^{0.28})$ when $k=2$ and $O(p^{0.36})$ when $k=3$ under an assumption in the spirit of Zaremba's Conjecture on continued fractions. This is an improvement on the more general attacks of Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter which have average-case time complexity $O(\sqrt{p})$. For any $k$, the average-case time complexity of our attack is $O(p^{1-δ_k+o(1)})$ where $δ_k$ is the Hausdorff dimension of a certain Cantor set. This tends to $O(\sqrt{p})$ as $k\to\infty$, so our attack has time complexity comparable to Mullan-Tsaban and Slaughter's attacks as $k$ grows. We give examples of collisions for large primes found by our attack when $k=2, 3$.

papers.title: Sufficient Dimension Reduction with Multimodal Predictor Objects
papers.abstract: We study the regression of a scalar response $Y$ on a Euclidean predictor $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^p$ and a random predictor object $\mathcal{Z}$ in a general metric space under arbitrary structural dependence. We introduce a joint sufficient dimension reduction $(\mathbf{B}^\top\mathbf{X}, \mathcal{G}_Z)$ constructed via a sequential conditional independence framework, which differs fundamentally from the ordinary central subspace of $Y \mid \mathbf{X}$. Methodologically, $\mathcal{Z}$ is embedded into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and a regularized kernel-response envelope model extracts a finite-dimensional reduction of the feature map. Partial adaptive estimation then recovers the Euclidean reduction conditional on the first-stage coordinates. We establish root-$n$ consistency rates for the first-stage envelope subspace under a shrinking regularizer, alongside large-sample consistency for the second-stage Euclidean subspace estimator. Simulations and two real-data applications illustrate the utility and flexibility of the proposed method.

papers.title: A proof of the constant-width numerical range conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Chien, Nakazato, and Meng that the numerical range of a finite complex matrix has constant width $d$ if and only if it is a closed disk of radius $d/2$, with a singleton allowed when $d=0$. For $d>0$, the characteristic polynomial of the associated Hermitian pencil and its translate by $d$ have a nonconstant common divisor over $\mathbb{C}(ζ)$. At points on the unit circle where the factorization can be evaluated, every root of the common divisor equals the smallest eigenvalue. A coefficient of the divisor thus gives a rational formula for that eigenvalue. The characteristic equation forces this rational function to be a Laurent polynomial with exponents in $\{-1,0,1\}$. Antipodal symmetry then makes the midpoint of the extreme eigenvalues a first harmonic, giving the support function of a disk. We also obtain the corresponding quadratic factor of the Kippenhahn polynomial.

papers.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are described by second-order tensor perturbations that contain free radiation together with a gauge-dependent response maintained by the scalar source. For a perfect fluid with constant equation of state $0<w<1$, we identify the free radiation with the out-state of the tensor perturbation, assembled from the light-cone residue of kernel functions for each pair of scalar modes. Its amplitudes follow from a classical LSZ-type reduction formula, in terms of the initial data and the light-cone-projected source. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: a redefinition of the tensor perturbation whose late-time shift has power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leaves these amplitudes unchanged. Transformations between intrinsic gauges, whose slice-normal observers and spatial coordinates are fixed by the matter and geometry without an external clock or independent oscillatory dynamics, are redefinitions of this kind, except on resonance surfaces of zero measure. The out-state is therefore the same in all intrinsic gauges, including the standard gauges of cosmological perturbation theory. The late-time Newtonian kernel is then the out-state kernel, which justifies its use for the energy spectrum of the free radiation. In matter domination, the out-state instead separates the free radiation from the static tidal response.

papers.title: A NURBS-enhanced high-order finite-volume method for compressible laminar boundary layers on curved domains with hybrid meshes
papers.abstract: High-fidelity simulation of compressible laminar boundary layers on curved domains requires physical wall boundary treatment and geometric representation compatible with high-order reconstruction, since viscous shear stresses and conductive heat fluxes are concentrated in a thin near-wall region. Conventional high-order methods often suffer from loss of accuracy near curved walls or require complicated wall treatments. To address these issues, in this paper, we develop a NURBS-enhanced $k$-exact finite-volume method for the steady compressible Navier--Stokes equations on hybrid meshes. To incorporate physical wall conditions into the high-order discretization, we develop a wall boundary treatment that employs sequential reconstruction without requiring the reconstruction variables to coincide with those used to prescribe the boundary conditions. The NURBS-based boundary representation is used to obtain a high-order accurate description of curved boundaries, and the diffusive generalized Riemann problem (dGRP) viscous flux is employed to enhance numerical robustness. A variety of numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the high-order accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: AdaFCP: Local Neural Functional Representations for Industrial Change Detection
papers.abstract: Industrial sensor measurements often form ordered functional profiles in which persistent operating-regime changes may be confined to short within-cycle regions. Fixed projections can dilute such changes, whereas data-adaptive representation learning complicates reliable statistical testing. This paper proposes adaptive functional change-point detection (AdaFCP) for retrospective detection of a single functional mean change. A compact window and neural basis learn a change-sensitive functional projection by matching the CUSUM path of projected scores to single-change templates. Standardized peak-CUSUM scanning then provides the detection statistic and transition estimate, while the fitted weights identify the contributing within-cycle region. Theoretical analysis characterizes the population path-matching signal and derives an optimal-direction signal-to-noise benchmark. Full-pipeline permutation calibration accounts for adaptive representation learning and restart selection, providing finite-sample false-positive control under exchangeability. A decision-preserving early-stopping variant, AdaFCP-ES, further reduces calibration effort without altering the fixed-budget test decision. Simulations demonstrate advantages over several fixed representations for localized oscillatory changes, while strong analytic and multiscale controls remain competitive. Applications to injection-molding pressure profiles and a nuisance-matched hydraulic benchmark illustrate transition localization and interpretable within-cycle diagnostics, while highlighting the need for dependence-aware calibration in naturally ordered industrial data.

papers.title: Real-time spectral combs from delayed quantum feedback in multimode cavity QED
papers.abstract: We study the time-dependent physical spectrum of light for a two-level atom coupled to a large, but discrete, number of modes of an electromagnetic cavity. Radiation emitted by the atom, placed at the center of the cavity, returns after the round-trip time $t_r$, re-excites it, and is re-emitted, producing a sequence of atomic population revivals. For a coupling approximately flat over the atomic linewidth, the emission dynamics reduces to a delay-differential equation of Bixon--Jortner type. Using its analytical solution in terms of Laguerre polynomials, we investigate how successive emission and reabsorption cycles shape the time-dependent spectrum. The physical spectrum exhibits revivals during which a transient frequency comb of spacing $2π/t_r$ develops. The comb results from the quantum interference between successive emission stages; its teeth sit not at the cavity modes but at the resonances of the effective two half-cavities created by the resonantly reflecting atom. The visibility scales as $e^{-Γt_r}$ with the filter bandwidth $Γ$, and at long times the comb converges to the dressed-mode spectrum, which we also obtain analytically in quantitative agreement with exact diagonalization. We show that the physical spectrum resolves the feedback phase, to which the atomic population is insensitive in the regime of well-separated emission stages, and provides additional frequency-resolved signatures of the atomic position. We discuss two feasible experimental implementations of our results with transmons (artificial atoms) coupled to microwave and surface-acoustic-wave resonators.

papers.title: A Hierarchical View of Ecological Encounters
papers.abstract: Encounters between individuals, or between individuals and entities like vehicles, are central to understanding a host of topics in ecology and related fields. Problems of mate-finding, predator-prey interactions, pathogen spread, and animal interactions with infrastructure all hinge on encounters. Historically, however, encounters have been difficult to observe at scale, and the relevant theoretical frameworks---which ultimately derive from the ideal gas law---have been badly mismatched to the underlying biology. Here, we synthesize and provide ecological context for recent developments in mathematics, statistics, and physics that permit the inclusion of more biological realism into encounter-related models. We propose an encounters--interactions--outcomes hierarchical framework for organizing core concepts across a diverse range of ecological scenarios. Implemented as a hierarchical Bayesian model, our framework permits tight connections with multi-level ecological data relevant to the estimation of encounter rates and their downstream impacts on interactions and outcomes. Throughout, we emphasize how the ongoing revolution in animal biologging yields empirical datasets that can be employed to quantify otherwise inaccessible rate parameters and their dependencies. We conclude with a series of major open questions about encounters designed to spur conceptual and quantitative integration across models, data sources, and ecological levels of organization.

papers.title: Weak convergence orders for a fully discrete approximation of semilinear stochastic PDEs driven by multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the weak convergence of a fully discrete approximation for a class of semilinear stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) driven by multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise. The scheme combines a spectral Galerkin discretization in space with an exponential Euler discretization in time. Compared with single-noise settings, the simultaneous presence of continuous and jump perturbations introduces additional challenges arising from discontinuous trajectories, nonlocal jump operators, and their interaction with state-dependent multiplicative coefficients. To overcome these difficulties, we establish the exponential integrability of the numerical solution processes and refined moment estimates in negative Sobolev norms for the associated first- and second-order variational processes. Combining these estimates with a discrete-time approximation argument and Wiener--Poisson Malliavin calculus, we derive regularity estimates for the solutions of the Kolmogorov equations associated with the spatial Galerkin approximations. Based on these estimates, we obtain the temporal and spatial weak convergence orders arbitrarily close to one with respect to discretization parameters $τ$ and $λ_N^{-1}$, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first weak convergence result for a fully discrete approximation of semilinear SPDEs with simultaneous multiplicative Gaussian and Poisson noise.

papers.title: A cyclotomic Artin-Tate formula and sphere packing for K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: We give new necessary conditions on the Weil polynomial of a K3 surface over a finite field using techniques from the theory of sphere packing. By comparing the Artin-Tate formula over a finite extension, we derive a special values formula at roots of unity that involves the discriminant of the Frobenius coinvariant lattice. Known bounds on the minimum discriminants of even rootless lattices then imply nontrivial lower bounds on these special values. Applying these new conditions to Kedlaya and Sutherland's list of candidate Weil polynomials of K3 surfaces over the field with 2 elements rules out over 50% of the candidates.

papers.title: Obvious Group Manipulations and Top Trading Cycles
papers.abstract: We introduce a group version of non-obvious manipulability, which is stronger than the original definition by Troyan and Morrill (2020) and weaker than group strategy-proofness, and study its implications in Shapley-Scarf housing markets. We provide several characterizations of the Top Trading Cycles mechanism using the new condition.

papers.title: An Empirical Study on Improving LLM-Based Issue Classification through Domain-Informed Analysis
papers.abstract: Issue reports that describe Intrinsic Bugs, Extrinsic Bugs, and Not a Bug cases often use similar language, but they might point to different causes and require different maintenance actions. This makes three-way issue classification difficult for Large Language Models (LLMs), particularly when prompt-based refinements begin to plateau. We study whether domain-informed analysis of LLM outputs can improve classification beyond prompt modification alone. Using 428 manually labeled issue reports, we evaluate six LLMs across 18 prompt configurations and analyze 7,704 model-generated rationales to identify recurring failure patterns in how models justify predictions, use evidence, and handle conflicting information. We translate these findings into a multi-stage pipeline that separates bug validity from bug origin. The pipeline improves macro F1 and Extrinsic Bug recall for five of the six models. The strongest pipeline configuration reaches 0.827 accuracy and 0.757 Extrinsic Bug recall, improving over the best-accuracy prompt-only baseline by +1.2 and +7.5 pp, respectively. The decomposition further reveals that bug origin classification is more reliable than validity, indicating that the bug-validity decision accounts for most of the remaining error. These results show that expert failure analysis can support more reliable LLM-based software engineering classifiers.

papers.title: Context Types: Bunched Modalities for Unifying Safety and Reachability
papers.abstract: Most type systems are designed to verify safety properties: the judgement $e : τ$ holds if $e$ may evaluate to any value contained in the denotation of $τ$, but nothing more. More recent type systems have considered the complementary class of reachability properties: in these systems, the typing judgment holds if $e$ must be able to evaluate to every value denoted by $τ$, and possibly more. This paper introduces a refinement type system for higher-order functional programs where types can capture both safety and reachability properties. Simultaneously supporting both is challenging because each imposes different constraints on how variable bindings in a typing context are interpreted. We address this challenge by treating typing contexts as a kind of resource that mediates which capabilities are available when typing a program. We formalize this notion by developing a resource algebra of contextual capabilities and a bunched modal context logic over this algebra. We then interpret our type system in this logic, establishing soundness with respect to a denotational semantics that unifies safety and reachability guarantees within a single typing judgement.

papers.title: Rhythmic-Semantic Co-Speech Gestures for Emotional Dialogue in Robots
papers.abstract: Co-speech gestures can increase engagement and improve speech understanding. Yet, most data-driven robot systems generate either rhythmic beat-like motion or semantically meaningful iconic gestures, but not both. We present an emotion-aware rhythmic-semantic co-speech gesture system that generates iconic and beat behaviors in real time from text and the robot's internal emotional state. We formalize the task of beat-iconic gesture generation using emotion and propose lightweight models that predict iconic timing and intensity, then fill the remaining spans with emotion-conditioned beats at an appropriate intensity level. We train on the BEAT2 dataset and deploy the system on the social robot Haru. In an online user study with 60 participants, our method shows stronger speech-gesture alignment and is preferred over baseline methods.

papers.title: Fragment-Free Constraint Programming for the Preemptive Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem
papers.abstract: This article addresses the preemptive flexible job shop scheduling problem with makespan minimization (FJm | pmtn | C_max). We propose an exact constraint programming approach that completely avoids representing the processing fragments of an operation. Operations are placed in flexible time windows, where Horn's workload condition guarantees feasible preemptive scheduling, and Jackson's preemptive earliest-deadline-first rule reconstructs exact processing segments post-optimization in O(n log n) time per machine. To manage undecided machine assignments, we extend the PreemptiveNoOverlap global constraint to optional intervals within IBM ILOG CP Optimizer, performing overload checking and preemptive edge-finding in O(n log n) time while eliminating infeasible machine alternatives. The CP model is warm-started using a multi-round MILP assignment relaxation with Carlier's head-tail bounds and a window-based greedy heuristic. Extensive computational experiments on 276 pFJSSP benchmark instances and 78 pJSSP instances demonstrate that the proposed method significantly advances the state of the art. Within a 600~s time limit, it improves the upper bounds of the previously published logic-based Benders decomposition by 3.6% on average, increases the number of proven optimal pFJSSP instances from 102 to 180, and closes 74 instances for the first time (including the entire Barnes family). On the pJSSP under identical hardware conditions, it proves 67 of 78 instances optimal (compared to 51 by the baseline solver Mistral) and closes 9 of the 11 long-standing open problems.

papers.title: Unified Ott--Antonsen Framework for Stability and Bifurcations in Ring Swarmalators
papers.abstract: Swarmalators, a prototypical model that integrates temporal rhythms with spatial swarming, have been widely used to explore the collective dynamics observed in active-matter systems. Although numerical simulations have revealed a variety of collective states, a general theoretical framework for the stability and bifurcations of the states remains unavailable. Here, by the model of one-dimensional ring-structured swarmalators with general distributions of natural frequencies and velocities, we conduct a systematic theoretical analysis of the stability and bifurcations of four representative collective states observed in simulations: the desynchronization state, the phase-wave state, the synchronization state, and the mixed state. We show that the macroscopic dynamics are governed by a low-dimensional invariant manifold, namely the generalized Ott--Antonsen manifold, and further establish that the same manifold underlies the collective dynamics of high-dimensional agent models, thereby unifying these seemingly different descriptions within a common reduction framework. Building on this connection, we derive stability conditions and bifurcation boundaries for the collective states and construct a bifurcation diagram in the two-parameter coupling plane, with theoretical predictions validated by large-scale numerical simulations. Our results clarify the dynamical origins of state selection in swarmalator systems and provide a theoretical foundation for analyzing nonequilibrium phase transitions in active-matter systems with coupled internal rhythms and spatial motions.

papers.title: Quantum-walk transport oracles and amplitude estimation of a scalar range statistic in proton therapy
papers.abstract: Quantum amplitude estimation (QAE) promises a quadratic reduction in the sampling cost of Monte Carlo (MC) particle transport, but two obstacles have kept it from radiotherapy physics: the lack of an efficient unitary encoding of charged-particle transport, and the mismatch between QAE's single-scalar output and the per-voxel structure of dose calculation. We address both. We construct a discrete-time quantum-walk transport oracle for protons in which an energy register is driven by an energy-dependent coin encoding a continuous-slowing-down surrogate of the stopping power, so that stochastic energy loss and range straggling follow from the circuit dynamics. The oracle is unitary, with one fresh coin qubit per step, and its gate count grows linearly in the number of energy levels. On it we formulate a scalar range statistic, the probability that a proton penetrates beyond a distal depth threshold, as a directly marked amplitude, and estimate it by maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation (MLQAE) with Grover iterations and finite shots. The oracle reproduces a Bragg-shaped depth-deposit profile agreeing with a classical MC of identical rules to within 0.27%, and Grover amplification matches $\sin^2((2k+1)θ)$ to machine precision up to $k=32$. At matched budget the MLQAE error falls as $N^{-0.93}$ against $N^{-0.49}$ for sampling, 4.8 times smaller at the largest budget. A three-gate resource analysis (output structure, amortization, error-corrected wall-clock) finds full dose maps structurally unfavourable irrespective of hardware, and the scalar statistic short of a wall-clock crossover at clinical scale: the oracle's derived cost of $1.0 \times 10^6$ logical gates per call ($3.5 \times 10^7$ with rotation synthesis), dominated by the multiplexed coin, is 160 to 5400 times the permitted budget. We report the reduction that would be required and identify the term responsible for it.

papers.title: Hopfion Superlattices in 3D Twisted Moiré Light Fields
papers.abstract: Moiré superlattices have recently been extended from electronic materials to photonic systems, enabling complex topological light fields such as skyrmion bags. However, these realizations remain confined to two dimensions. Here, we demonstrate 3D moiré superlattices formed by twisting multi-volume spatiotemporal optical lattices, giving rise to previously undiscovered 3D quasiparticle topologies, including hopfion bags, hopfion quasicrystals, and hopfion-hopfionium nested superlattices. By tailoring the interference polarization textures of the moiré spacetime lattices, we achieve controlled topological transitions among these states, and tailored topological numbers of hopfion bags. These spatiotemporal supertopologies offer a promising platform for high-capacity information encoding in higher dimensions.

papers.title: Leveraging Psychophysical Attentional Distribution for Gaze-Augmented Reward Modeling
papers.abstract: Integrating human feedback into language models has gained increasing attention as a means to align model outputs with human preferences, with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) serving as a prominent framework for preference-based alignment. Recent studies have incorporated eye-tracking (ET) data as an additional supervisory signal for reward model training, grounding reward learning in human reading behavior. Building on this approach, we extend prior fixation-centric models by leveraging established findings from cognitive psychology on human letter recognition. Specifically, we model visual attention as a spatially graded distribution centered on the current gaze location and incorporate this representation into reward model training. Our results show that the reward model trained with the proposed gaze distribution achieves higher preference prediction accuracy than a baseline model. Moreover, some results from our experiments are qualitatively consistent with established findings on human attention during reading, suggesting that they potentially capture cognitively meaningful aspects of human attention allocation.

papers.title: Half-inverse problems for perturbed Bessel operators with a known left-hand potential
papers.abstract: For the regular Sturm-Liouville operator $-\frac{{\rm d}^2}{{\rm d}x^2}+q$ acting in $L^2(0,1)$, the Hochstadt-Lieberman theorem states that one full spectrum together with the potential on either the left half-interval $q|_{(0,1/2)}$ or the right half-interval $q|_{(1/2,1)}$ uniquely determines the full potential $q$. The inverse-square singular term $\tfrac{l(l+1)}{x^2}$ in the perturbed Bessel operator $-\frac{{\rm d}^2}{{\rm d}x^2}+\frac{l(l+1)}{x^2}+q$, acting in $L^2(0,1)$, breaks the left-right symmetry. It is known that, when the right half of the potential $q|_{(1/2,1)}$ is given, the uniqueness of the potential can be established even if a finite number of eigenvalues (depending on $l$) are omitted. In this paper we study the opposite setting--where the left half potential $q|_{(0,1/2)}$ is known--and show that one full spectrum together with finitely many norming constants uniquely determine the full potential $q$. Moreover, we specify the minimum number of norming constants required for the uniqueness. Finally, for positive integer $l$, $L^2$ potentials, and the Dirichlet boundary condition at $x = 1$, we establish the local bi-Lipschitz stability and the local solvability from the full spectrum and finitely many norming constants, assuming the potential on the left half-interval is fixed.

papers.title: Log-Concavity in Narayana Transforms and Stack-Sorting Fibers
papers.abstract: Given a permutation $π$ of size $n$, let $D_π(x)$ denote the descent polynomial of the fiber of $π$ under West's stack-sorting map. We prove that $D_π(x)$ is ultra-log-concave of order $n-1$ and, therefore, log-concave. More generally, we prove that a multivariate refinement of $D_π(x)$ recording ascent tops and descent tops is the basis generating polynomial of a laminar matroid. We deduce a result about simplex integration from Brändén and Huh's theory and apply it to weighted matchings, obtaining a refinement of the log-concavity of $D_π(x)$ that incorporates the peak statistic on the stack-sorting fiber of $π$. These results imply the log-concavity of certain sums of products of Narayana polynomials over the lattice points of integral binary nestohedra. A complementary argument shows that replacing the monomials of a homogeneous real-stable polynomial with nonnegative coefficients by products of shifted Narayana polynomials produces a real-rooted polynomial; we discuss several applications. The results in this paper were formalized in Lean by AxiomProver.

papers.title: Sharp Sample Complexity of KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: KL-regularized reinforcement learning, the objective behind maximum-entropy RL and RL from human feedback, is variational inference in the graphical model of "control as inference": the regularized optimal policy is a posterior over trajectories, and the suboptimality of a policy is $β$ times a KL divergence between path measures. However, it is not known how many samples it takes to learn this posterior, even with a generative model. Earlier $1/ε$ guarantees scale with $H^5$ in the effective horizon $H$, and no lower bound for MDPs depends on the temperature $β$. In this work, we show that for a discounted MDP with $K$ state-action pairs, the plug-in estimator finds a policy that is $ε$-optimal from every initial state with $\widetilde{O}(KH^3/(ε\max\{ε,β\}) + KH)$ samples, and that no algorithm, even one that chooses where to sample, can do with fewer when $ε\lesssim \min\{H, H^2/β\}$. For $ε< β$ this is a $1/ε$ rate with the same horizon dependence as unregularized RL. We also find the exact asymptotic constant of the plug-in estimator, a Fisher-weighted variance of the estimated soft Q-function. The estimator is locally asymptotically minimax among methods that sample every pair equally often, and we give the allocation of samples that is optimal among adaptive designs. Simulations on small MDPs match the rates and the constants.

papers.title: Euclidean Hulls of Double Cyclic Codes of Arbitrary Block Lengths
papers.abstract: Gao et al. \cite{GWF23} recently explored the Euclidean hulls of double cyclic codes over $\mathbb{Z}_2$. While they found answers for non-separable codes with coprime lengths ($\gcd(r, s) = 1$), the non-coprime case ($\gcd(r, s) > 1$) remained an open question. This paper completely solves that problem for all possible block lengths. We calculate the exact generator polynomials for the hull and show the precise conditions needed for a non-separable code to turn into a separable one. Using this, we show how to construct non-separable LCD codes. We also include several numerical examples to confirm our findings.

papers.title: ExRL: Sample-Efficient Online Adaptation of Long-Chunk Policies via Execution Length Control
papers.abstract: Predicting long action chunks, often spanning dozens of timesteps, has become a key ingredient in increasingly capable robot policies. In this paper, we find that adapting these long-chunk policies with existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods can require many online samples due to the high dimensionality of the action chunks being optimized, making such adaptation impractical in real-world scenarios where interaction data are costly to collect. Our key insight is to shift adaptation from optimizing actions to optimizing how long to execute each predicted action chunk. This keeps the adaptation space low-dimensional while its expressivity grows with the chunk size. We thus introduce Execution at the Right Length (ExRL), a simple approach which augments the base policy with a lightweight adapter that predicts the execution length of each chunk and is trained using off-policy RL algorithms. Across simulation benchmarks and real-world robotic tasks, ExRL enables sample-efficient adaptation of a diverse range of long-chunk policies with minimal task-specific hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: Coupled Cluster Simulations of Vibrational Circular Dichroism Spectra
papers.abstract: We report the first simulations of vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) spectra at the coupled-cluster level of theory. Using a generalization of Stephens's pioneering magnetic-field perturbation theory framework for the magnetic-dipole vibrational transition moment to biorthonormal wave functions, we have derived generalized expressions for the corresponding atomic axial tensors (AATs) and velocity-gauge atomic polar tensors that collapse to Stephens's expressions for real, Hermitian states. Adapting these exact-state expressions to coupled-cluster left- and right-hand biorthonormal wave functions and using our recently developed density-based formulation yields compact equations that involve only perturbed ground-state amplitudes, as well as unperturbed and perturbed, unrelaxed one-electron densities; two-electron-density contributions vanish exactly. We have validated the resulting AATs by comparison with our previous configuration interaction formulation for a two-electron system, size-intensivity tests, a translational sum rule, and other tests. Simulated VCD spectra for (S)-3-chloro-1-butyne at the coupled-cluster singles and doubles level with the correlation-consistent triple-zeta basis set reveal significant discrepancies between length and velocity gauges. We find that the addition of large-exponent functions via a core-valence basis set for the Hartree--Fock reference components yields substantially improved gauge invariance without the need for gauge-including atomic orbitals.

papers.title: Boundary dualities of symplectic Chern-Simons theories and minimal models
papers.abstract: We propose that a Neumann-type boundary condition of the 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ $USp(2n)$ Chern-Simons theory at the level $-(n+\frac32)$ with a fundamental chiral multiplet is dual to a Dirichlet-type boundary condition of an Abelian rank-$0$ theory. In a topological twist we propose that it supports the affine vertex operator algebra (VOA) $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2))$. With the corresponding specialization of the fugacities, the line defect half-indices of the antisymmetric Wilson lines give, up to monomials, the supercharacters of all its modules, which coincide up to signs with the characters of the Virasoro minimal model $M(2,2n+3)$. We extend the duality to the level $-(n+\ell+\frac12)$ and propose that the boundary VOA is $L_n(\mathfrak{osp}(1|2\ell))$. Together with the Giveon-Kutasov type duality and the mirror symmetry, the proposed dualities form a web of dualities of the boundary conditions and the line operators. For other gauge groups with real matter we propose that the boundary VOA in the holomorphic twist is the commutant of the gauge currents in free real fermions, which is the Ising model for $Spin(7)$ with the spinor and the $\mathcal N=1$ superconformal minimal model $SM(3,5)$ for $G_2$ with $\mathbf7$.

papers.title: Differentially Private Statistical Inference for Rankings from Pairwise Comparisons
papers.abstract: Reliable inference for rankings of large language models based on human pairwise comparisons must preserve the privacy of individual preference records. To meet this need, we develop methods for score and rank inference under the Bradley-Terry model with edge differential privacy. For an objective-perturbed estimator, a new leave-one-out analysis establishes finite-sample bounds on Euclidean and entrywise estimation errors. For sufficiently dense comparison graphs, the error bounds extend to smaller privacy budgets, including regimes in which its privacy term dominates its statistical term. A uniform asymptotic expansion yields asymptotically valid confidence intervals for individual scores and pairwise score differences. To improve finite-sample performance, we account for both regularization bias and privacy-induced randomness by combining a plug-in ridge-bias correction with Gaussian-Laplace calibration. We further establish a bootstrap procedure for simultaneous rank inference, providing asymptotically valid confidence sets for individual ranks and tests of top-$K$ membership. When the comparison probability is public and known, all proposed inferential procedures require no additional privacy budget. We evaluate finite-sample performance through simulations and apply the proposed methods to rank large language models for creative writing.

papers.title: Hand-Object Contact Transition Detection in Egocentric Video
papers.abstract: This paper tackles the task of hand-object contact transition detection in egocentric video, which aims to localize the two temporal boundaries of a contact episode: the moment a hand first establishes contact with an object (touch) and the moment contact is released (release). We propose a unified framework that jointly models the interacting hand and object to accurately localize both transition types. The proposed framework augments hand-centric spatiotemporal representations with object-aware features learned directly from the video and introduces a transition-aware event spotting formulation tailored to contact transitions, without relying on external object or hand-object interaction detectors during inference. To support this task, we present ContactTransition, a dataset comprising 4,021 egocentric videos with 8,498 touch and 8,077 release annotations, together with object-of-interest supervision. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms strong two-stage and end-to-end event-spotting baselines on both transition types. Finally, we show that detected contact transitions provide effective temporal anchors for downstream egocentric hand-object reasoning.

papers.title: The WoW: A Large-Scale World Knowledge Corpus for Full-Lifecycle LLM Training
papers.abstract: Existing Chinese educational corpora often suffer from fragmented coverage and a lack of systematic organization. In this paper, we propose WoW (\textbf{Wo}rld Kno\textbf{w}ledge), a large-scale dataset designed for the full-cycle training of foundation models. The construction of this dataset is driven by an Educational Knowledge Graph, which serves as a taxonomic backbone for the systematic collection and completion of missing educational modules across all levels. Compared to previous versions, this iteration provides enhanced systematicity, superior quality, and a larger scale, while incorporating multimodal signals and supporting every stage of model development. Experiments demonstrate that WoW significantly improves model performance across diverse benchmarks. To facilitate community research, we further provide an interactive platform for graph-based data selection and retrieval.

papers.title: When Reconstruction Helps Event-Camera Person Triggers
papers.abstract: Event cameras record asynchronous changes in brightness. To use a general visual model as a recording trigger, a system must represent these measurements in a form the model can interpret. We compare direct grayscale accumulation, two temporal encodings, and two intensity reconstructors on paired real event data. On 192 windows from four held-out DSEC recordings, thresholds calibrated only on development data yielded 40 of 52 person detections and 12 of 140 background positives with E2VID. The strongest direct temporal encoding at an admissible fixed cutoff yielded 14 detections and seven background positives. A retrospective comparison at a common 10% background-positive cap yielded 40 detections for E2VID and at most 19 for any direct encoding. FireNet+ had lower preparation cost and produced 21 detections with zero observed background positives at its frozen cutoff. On the same 192 windows, Qwen3-VL-4B yielded 33/52, 2/140 with E2VID and 9/52, 9/140 with the highest-recall direct rendering, the three-bin image (person detections, background positives). A 96-second exploratory replay illustrates the sensitivity of episode capture and recording starts to cutoff selection. The experiments identify a detection benefit from reconstruction under controlled input history and distinguish it from the cost and false starts of continuous triggering.

papers.title: Simultaneous Near-Optimal Region Identification in Continuous Simulation Optimization: Minimax Complexity and Adaptive Sampling
papers.abstract: Simulation optimization typically returns a single estimated optimal point. When decisions also depend on criteria evaluated independently of simulation, such as resource cost, the decision maker instead needs the set of designs whose expected performance lies within a tolerance of the optimum, often choosing the tolerance only after seeing the tradeoffs. We study how to identify these near-optimal regions on a continuous design space, simultaneously for all tolerances up to a prescribed maximum $T$, with region estimation error at most $η$. We show that region identification is not a by-product of optimization. Specifically, when $α>ν$, any procedure, even one given the optimal design in advance, needs at least $Ω\bigl(η^{-(2+d/ν)}\min\{1,KT^{d/α}\}\bigr)$ simulation evaluations, where $d$ is the dimension, $ν$ the smoothness, and $(K,α)$ the covering parameters that describe the geometry of the near-optimal designs. We propose SASORI, which returns an estimated optimal point and the regions for all tolerances from the same evaluations, matching this lower bound up to logarithmic factors. SASORI also achieves the optimal tradeoff between region estimation error and cumulative regret, and reduces to a minimax-optimal simulation optimization procedure at zero tolerance. Numerical experiments illustrate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

papers.title: Design and Over-the-Air Evaluation of a Digital Twin-Driven Site-Specific Neural Receiver for 5G NR on NVIDIA DGX Spark
papers.abstract: We design and evaluate a site-specific neural receiver for the 5G New Radio (NR) uplink. A corridor digital twin built from a radar scan and refined manually provides 28,671 ray-traced channel records for training an eight-round convolutional graph neural network with pilot-aware inputs and auxiliary channel supervision. The GPU on NVIDIA DGX Spark evaluates time--frequency convolutions in parallel across the received grid to accelerate inference. The receiver uses the standard NR uplink waveform and reference signals and feeds soft bits to the existing transport-block decoder. In over-the-air tests with NI USRP B210 radios under common radio settings, the site-trained receiver achieves the highest mean uplink rate at all five positions. At a non-line-of-sight corner, it reaches 16.2 Mb/s, compared with 4.1 Mb/s for the conventional receiver and 2.4 Mb/s for the 3GPP-trained neural receiver. These results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating neural reception into the 5G NR physical layer and show its potential for AI-RAN deployments.

papers.title: Data-Efficient Unlearning-Based Backdoor Detection in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Detecting backdoor attacks in federated learning (FL) is challenging because malicious clients can manipulate the global model while preserving main-task performance. Static model-update statistics may therefore fail to clearly distinguish malicious from benign clients. Unlearning-based detectors instead probe client models through loss ascent on clean server data, but detection performance degrades with scarce proxy data. We propose Screening via Unlearning Response Analysis (SURA), a data-efficient detector. SURA reuses the same small clean proxy across multiple train-mode loss-ascent steps, strengthening client responses without additional clean data. For federated vision models with batch normalization (BN), repeated probing also changes BN running statistics and can confound endpoint measurements. SURA addresses this by restoring the shared pre-probe BN state only at readout while preserving the parameter changes induced by probing. This separates repeated probing from response measurement and removes BN drift and the interaction between parameter and BN-state changes from the readout. Across six backdoor attacks, SURA uses only 10 clean server images, outperforms methods under the same data budget, and approaches the robustness obtained with much larger proxy sets.

papers.title: Pseudo-marginal Sampling for Selective Inference
papers.abstract: Inference after adaptive selection must account for selection bias. One approach is to condition on the selected event, but for complex selection procedures, the resulting conditional distribution can be analytically intractable and require sampling-based methods. Rejection sampling provides a natural baseline: it repeatedly draws from a proposal and retains only samples that reproduce the observed selection. This can be prohibitively expensive when the selection event is rare. We address this computational bottleneck with a pseudo-marginal Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that samples from the selective distribution. Using a weak Poincaré inequality, we analyze its computational efficiency relative to rejection sampling and identify when it can offer substantial gains. In the classical file-drawer problem, we derive precise computational costs for both methods, illustrating exponential improvement as the selection event becomes increasingly rare. In numerical experiments involving complex selection procedures without tractable conditional distributions, the pseudo-marginal sampler is often hundreds of times more efficient than rejection sampling, while the resulting tests achieve nominal selective Type I error.

papers.title: On the two-component $b$-family system modeling shallow-water waves of medium amplitude
papers.abstract: We formally derive a two-component $b$-family system from the full governing equations for two-dimensional water waves in the medium-amplitude regime. The system contains higher-order nonlinearities and includes a two-component Camassa-Holm type system for equatorial shallow-water waves with the Coriolis effect as a special case. We establish the local well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in $B^{s-1}_{p,r}\times B^s_{p,r}$ with $s>\max\{1+\frac1p,\frac32\}$. Using Littlewood-Paley theory and Osgood's lemma, we also prove local well-posedness in the critical Besov space $B^{\frac12}_{2,1}\times B^{\frac32}_{2,1}$. Furthermore, we derive a blow-up criterion for strong solutions. For a special choice of the parameters, we prove finite-time blow-up for a class of initial data and provide an upper bound for the maximal existence time.

papers.title: Route-Time Conflict Maps for Cooperative End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Existing cooperative end-to-end driving works at Class A (status-sharing) of the SAE J3216 classes of cooperative driving automation (CDA): vehicles exchange what they perceive, not what they intend, so each plans alone when to go, which limits cooperation and leads to deadlock when both vehicles yield or to collisions when both go. We present When2Go, a cooperative end-to-end driving system that learns when to go by sharing intent under CDA Class B or higher. Each vehicle broadcasts its LiDAR detections with forecast motion as instance tokens, together with its plan and intended trajectory. The receiver draws the fused detections, forecasts and partner plans into a route-time conflict map, the occupancy along its route over the planning horizon, on which a planner scores candidate speed profiles. Where two intended trajectories conflict, an order gate, a precedence network distilled from a right-of-way rule, decides who goes first; both vehicles evaluate it on the same messages and so reach the same order. When2Go imitates the rule-based expert of V2Xverse, which sees the simulator's ground truth; stops that When2Go cannot observe within its 2 s planning horizon are relabelled, so that it does not learn to wait without an observable cause. For our runs only, the benchmarks' PID controller steers by When2Go's waypoints instead of the route, and its forced push of long-waiting vehicles is off. With one model, When2Go sets the state of the art on three closed-loop CARLA benchmarks: 97.8 and 90.7 driving score on InterDrive without and with traffic (best published 90.1 and 78.9), 70.0 on the public V2Xverse protocol (best of sixteen rerun methods 59.1) and 88.2 on MDrive (best rerun 85.1), with 95.0% of its vehicles collision-free (87.7%).

papers.title: The Largest Ground Set for Sunflower-Free Systems
papers.abstract: We construct the largest $r$-flower-free system of $k$-uniform sets for $k=3, r=4$ where every element of the ground set $G$ is used at least once. The goal is to maximize $|G|$, also called the span. We define $\mathrm{sp}(k, r)$ to be the maximum $|G|$ for such a system. We show that $\mathrm{sp}(3, 4) = 39$, which yields an improved upper bound $f(3, 4) \leq 130$, improving upon the Erdős--Rado bound of $f(3, 4) \leq 162$.

papers.title: Reasoning-Aware Relational Representation Learning for Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation
papers.abstract: Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation (OV-SGG) requires models to recognize visual relationships beyond the training vocabulary, yet existing methods often rely on dataset-specific object--predicate co-occurrence patterns. Under long-tailed distributions and noisy object localization, such reliance leads to biased, entangled relation representations, limiting both rare-relation recognition and generalization to unseen predicates. To address these challenges, we propose RaRe, a reasoning-aware relational representation learning framework that transforms MLLM-generated chain-of-thought (CoT) rationales into structured relation embeddings. Rather than using CoT only as an intermediate reasoning trace for final prediction, RaRe directly optimizes the rationale-derived representation space to improve inter-relation discriminability. Specifically, RaRe first aligns rationale embeddings with textualized relation descriptions through self-supervised contrastive learning, and then refines rationale generation with a specificity-oriented reinforcement learning objective that encourages semantically object-pair-specific relational evidence. Experiments on VG150 and PSG demonstrate improved category-balanced recognition over existing baselines, while the additional gains from learning vary across datasets and proposal settings. Code available at: https://artanic30.github.io/project_pages/RaRe.

papers.title: Impact of Reduced-Order Modelling on Sum-of-Squares Region-of-Attraction Certification for Grid-Forming and Grid-Following Converters
papers.abstract: With the increasing penetration of power-electronic equipment, the transient stability of grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) converters is increasingly characterized through the region of attraction (ROA) of the post-fault equilibrium. Sum-of-squares (SOS) programming yields certified inner approximations of the ROA, yet its computational cost grows rapidly with system order. Reduced-order models are therefore widely used to reduce computational cost and, more importantly, to enable analytical investigation. However, ROA analyses based on these models often assume that reproducing the converter's transient response, or retaining more dynamics in the correct time-frame, is sufficient to preserve the ROA of the full-order system. Using time-domain ODE simulations as a reference, the SOS-based ROA of each reduced-order GFM and GFL model is assessed against both its own simulated ROA and that of the corresponding full-order model, thereby separating SOS-induced conservativeness from model-order-induced ROA distortion. The results indicate that increasing reduced-order model complexity does not necessarily improve SOS-based ROA fidelity. In the cases examined, more complex reduced-order models yield lower SOS coverage of the full-order reference ROA, despite closer ODE-boundary agreement in some regions. Model selection should therefore consider both full-order ROA fidelity and certified coverage of the practical operating range, rather than model complexity alone.

papers.title: Evaluating Compositional Generalization in Transformers: The Role of Composition Equivalence and Module Coverage
papers.abstract: Compositional generalization is an important form of out-of-distribution generalization, defined as the ability to train on some combinations of modules (e.g., functions such as sort, filter) and then generalize to unseen combinations. Despite substantial empirical work evaluating compositional generalization in transformers, findings have been inconsistent because evaluations were often conducted on a limited set of train-test splits, defined in an ad hoc manner. Through a systematic evaluation, we identify two key aspects of the train-test distribution that strongly affect performance: composition equivalence and module coverage. We show that the apparent performance of direct models (trained only on final outputs) results primarily from exploiting composition equivalences, meaning different sequences of modules that reduce to identical end-to-end functions. When benchmarks eliminate these equivalences, performance drops significantly, showing their inability to generalize to compositions of known modules that produce novel end-to-end functions. We further demonstrate that performance degrades monotonically as module coverage shifts increase (when modules appear in different contexts between train and test), affecting both direct and step-by-step models (trained on intermediate and final outputs). These findings have concrete implications for benchmark design: benchmarks that include compositional equivalences can lead to significant overestimation of the generalization abilities of direct models, and benchmarks that include both module coverage violations and compositional equivalences can exacerbate shortcut learning. As a case study, we demonstrate the role of compositional equivalence on the generalization performance of the pre-trained model Llama3-8B on the code-output prediction task in the coding benchmark LiveCodeBench.

papers.title: DeRep: Learning Depth Representations for End-to-End Navigation in Cluttered Environments
papers.abstract: End-to-end navigation in cluttered environments relies on compact visual representations to support collision avoidance and goal-directed motion. Existing methods typically learn these representations jointly with the policy or through observation reconstruction, which does not explicitly specify what information the representation should preserve. Moreover, they are usually evaluated with a single downstream policy learner, although the benefit of a representation may depend on how the policy is learned. It therefore remains unclear how different representation-learning objectives affect downstream navigation performance and robustness. This work proposes DeRep, a navigation-oriented representation-learning method that combines local bird's-eye-view reachability supervision with depth reconstruction. To compare representation objectives under controlled conditions, we pretrain encoders with a common architecture and freeze them during downstream learning. We evaluate the representations using a linear policy probe, flow-matching imitation learning, and reinforcement learning with PPO. DeRep achieves the lowest linear policy probe prediction error and outperforms reconstruction alone across all six tested PPO conditions. In imitation learning, both reachability-based objectives achieve higher mean success rates than reconstruction alone, with similar mean success rates between the reachability-only and joint objectives. These results demonstrate consistent benefits of incorporating reachability supervision into depth representation pretraining across different downstream learning methods and evaluation conditions. We further deploy the PPO policy with the frozen DeRep encoder in Gazebo and on a physical quadrotor without fine-tuning, demonstrating its capability for zero-shot sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfer.

papers.title: Facilitated Relaxation Overrides Energetic Pathways in a Multiphase Square-Kagome Artificial Spin Ice
papers.abstract: Relaxation in interacting many-body systems is typically assumed to follow energy minimization, yet local dynamical rules can determine which microscopic pathways are accessible. In facilitated relaxation, these pathways are enabled or blocked by neighboring configurations. However, isolating such rules in natural materials is difficult because energetics, disorder and dynamics are usually entangled. Here we realize a geometrically tunable square-kagome artificial spin ice-a lithographic nanomagnet array-that provides a clean, designable platform for facilitated relaxation. The array hosts two tunable nearest-neighbor interactions and supports multiple low-energy phases: spin crystal, spin liquid and spin foam. In the spin-foam phase, abundant facilitator configurations allow relaxation to follow Boltzmann statistics. In the spin-crystal phase, by contrast, domain-wall excitations are trapped in non-Boltzmann distributions, although energetically preferred relaxation channels exist. The ordered crystal background lacks the facilitators needed to connect topologically distinct domain-wall classes. These classes are therefore kinetically isolated, as observed in both experiment and Monte Carlo simulation. Our results show that transition-network topology can override energetic relaxation, establishing artificial spin ice as a programmable platform for constrained dynamics and nonergodic relaxation.

papers.title: Failure of endpoint estimates for lacunary bilinear spherical maximal functions on Heisenberg groups
papers.abstract: We prove that the lacunary bilinear Nevo--Thangavelu spherical maximal operator on the Heisenberg group $\mathbb H^n$ does not map $H^1(\mathbb H^n)\times H^1(\mathbb H^n)$ into $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb H^n)$ for any $n\geq1$. We obtain this result by lifting the Euclidean counterexample in our recent result (arXiv:2610.40100) to the Heisenberg group.

papers.title: Thermal-pulse-resolved Binary Population Synthesis with Detailed Stellar Models: Implications for Long-period WD+MS Formation
papers.abstract: The origin of the long-orbital-period white dwarf--main-sequence (WD+MS) binaries revealed by Gaia challenges the traditional association of common-envelope evolution (CEE) with short orbital periods. We develop a thermal-pulse-resolved binary population synthesis framework based on 51 detailed MESA evolutionary tracks with initial masses of 1--6 $M_{\odot}$. Applying these tracks to $5\times10^6$ initially sampled binaries, we follow the time-dependent stellar radius, wind mass loss, angular momentum, and tidal interactions, while calculating the envelope binding energy directly from the donor structure at the onset of Roche-lobe overflow.
